trace.claim: Current world velocity/acceleration are rotated into current body basis; retained earlier observation.velocity and smoothed local acceleration are reused without a stored basis.
Deceleration scale tests a dot product of previous velocity and current filtered acceleration, and compares current/previous planar speeds.
Stored BodyObservation holds tick and local velocity only; no world velocity or prior orientation accompanies it.

connections.condition_and_consequence: For an otherwise eligible response episode with turning between observations and relevant nonzero vectors, previous and current body-local components can refer to different bases, changing the braking classification/scale. Eligibility excludes reset cases such as discontinuity, action, posture transition, airborne and raised guard. Actual supported turn rates, timing and observed visual effects remain unproved; response is presentation only. Smoothed acceleration frame semantics is a connected policy question, not a second automatic defect.
connections.future_direction: Preserve or reconstruct the spatial frame so compared observations share a basis; decide intended response-filter frame separately, retaining validated numeric guards and by-value state commit. Central owns the ledger and remediation.

lenses.name: producer-propagation
lenses.assessment: Typed config → current target → checked candidate → body/pelvis presentation, and current fixed-clock capture path → skeleton tick traced only in registered windows.

lenses.name: existing-type-owners
lenses.assessment: Velocity, acceleration, angular magnitude, response rates and sample ticks have explicit bespoke owners; BodyLocalVelocity alone does not carry the orientation that gives its frame.

lenses.name: admission-contracts
lenses.assessment: Config validates response margin/gap; typed values check finite and nonnegative inputs. Positive reference can still lack sufficient operation-level range; supported application tuning needs decision.

lenses.name: invariant-operations
lenses.assessment: Ratio before finite angle clamp and cross-frame dot product reconnect two distinct existing issues. Spring checks intermediate values and velocity norm before cap.

lenses.name: aggregate-states
lenses.assessment: Observation tick, velocity and frame basis, and current filtered acceleration must be related at comparison; guard/reset state and candidate commit delimit supported cases.

lenses.name: type-ownership
lenses.assessment: Observation/response owner governs frame identity; config owns tuning and native animation operations consume it. No product or foreign type rewrite proposed.

lenses.name: redundant-authority
lenses.assessment: Stored target, response and angular velocity represent different dynamics rather than automatic duplicate truth. Frame rotation is missing from retained observation; do not conflate with clock identities.

lenses.name: behavior-preservation
lenses.assessment: Two P16 source bodies are exactly identical to 95e/a120/6533/039, established by bytes, but snapshot histories and scopes differ; no behavior, validation or whole-snapshot equivalence established.

lenses.name: enum-shapes
lenses.assessment: First observation, discontinuity and reset branches express distinct legitimate modes; no unsupported enum conversion established.

lenses.name: derivability
lenses.assessment: No source-backed safe derive substitution established for these checked response APIs. Wider trait owners remain outside scope.

lenses.name: type-granularity
lenses.assessment: Typed local velocity versus acceleration and angular quantities preserve units but do not distinguish changing body bases; maintain physical vs presentation and source vs fixed clock identities.

lenses.name: magic-strings
lenses.assessment: Native diagnostic error strings and config field names are output/serialization boundaries; no business error-string classifier was established.

lenses.name: magic-numbers
lenses.assessment: Typed reference acceleration, rate, seconds, radians and sample span carry separate units. Report margin is a named validated numeric allowance; no raw-primitive finding inferred by syntax alone.
